subject: ACMEHealth private fleet: patch scheduling & rollback guardrails
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Harry Stevens <harry.stevens@acmehealth.com>, ACME IT Ops <ops-it@acmehealth.com>
Cc: DPO ACME <dpo@acmehealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed maintenance window and version pin plan for ACME private fleet

Hi Harry / ACME Ops team —

Following our runbook review last week, we are proposing a maintenance window to apply the 2026.11.1 security and runtime patches to your private fleet (pinned nodes). High level:

- Target maintenance window: Saturday 2026-12-04, 00:30–03:30 PT (3-hour window, with 60m warm/monitor after final slice)
- Scope: control-plane agent update + runtime micropatch, KV-cache compatibility checks, model-serving node lib updates
- Pinning approach: we will temporarily pin the fleet controller to v2026.10 for read-only traffic slicing, then stagger unpin to v2026.11.1 in 20% increments across slices

Key asks from ACME: confirmation of acceptable window, signoff on rollback criteria, and DPO acknowledgement for audit retention changes.

Attached: acme_patch_plan_v2.pdf (detailed steps), rollback_playbook.md (playbook), maintenance_risk_matrix.xlsx

If this window doesn't work we'll propose the following Saturday (12/11) same time — please confirm by EOD Wed so we can book canary resources.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Technical Account Lead, Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.com
[Attachment: acme_patch_plan_v2.pdf (3 pages)]
[Attachment: rollback_playbook.md (1.2 KB)]
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Harry Stevens <harry.stevens@acmehealth.com>, ACME IT Ops <ops-it@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed maintenance window and version pin plan for ACME private fleet

Thanks Rachel — quick ops notes from the runtime side:

- Recommend increasing the window to 4 hours (00:30–04:30 PT) to give extra time for slice-level verification and KV cache rehydration; real-world rehydrate observed ~18–25 minutes per 10% slice on similar workloads.
- Canary: allocate a 5-node canary (slice-0) in the same AZ as production control-plane to exercise both agent update and model-serving path under realistic traffic.
- Drain steps: we should perform a two-step KV drain (soft, then hard) to avoid cold-cache penalty spikes. The plan attached includes exact kubectl drains and grace windows.

I'll add the additional commands to INF-3421 and propose the 4-hour window unless ACME requests otherwise.

Jonas
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
[Inline: excerpt from maintenance_risk_matrix.xlsx — KV-rehydrate-time estimates]
From: Harry Stevens <harry.stevens@acmehealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, ACME IT Ops <ops-it@acmehealth.com>
Cc: DPO ACME <dpo@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Proposed maintenance window and version pin plan for ACME private fleet

Rachel / team —

Thanks for the detailed plan. A few items from ACME:

- Window timing: late-night is preferred. Saturday 12/04 works but we prefer 01:00–05:00 ET (which matches your 00:30–04:30 PT suggestion) — please state the exact UTC timestamps in the runbook.
- Audit/data locality: we need confirmation that none of the telemetry artifacts (detailed KV traces) leave our VPC and that audit logs for the maintenance event live in our S3 bucket for 90 days.
- Rollback SLA: our compliance team requires a maximum of 2 hours to restore pinned-in-place versions after a full rollback decision; is that achievable?

Also cc'd DPO — please advise on retention/audit needs.

Harry
Director, IT Ops — ACME Health
[External acknowledgement; will coordinate internal approvals]
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Harry Stevens <harry.stevens@acmehealth.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed maintenance window and version pin plan for ACME private fleet

Hi Harry — quick answers and proposed guardrails from Redwood:

- Telemetry/artifacts: maintenance-level telemetry (agent logs, upgrade traces) will be written to an ACME-owned S3 bucket (we will not copy debug-level KV payloads outside the VPC). We will provide the S3 path in the runbook and a signed pointer in the postmortem.
- Audit retention: we will configure lifecycle policy to retain event logs for 90 days as requested.
- Rollback SLA: 2-hour full rollback is tight but achievable if we pre-stage pinned images and pre-capture current control-plane snapshots. We will: 
  - Pre-push pinned images to your private registry 24 hours prior
  - Create control-plane snapshots and store in your S3 staging path
  - Reserve a rollback runbook with personnel assigned (Ops lead + SRE lead + TA)

Rollback triggers (proposed):
- >3% overall error rate on model-serving endpoints for 10 consecutive minutes
- p95 latency increase >200 ms sustained for 10 minutes
- Failing readiness/liveness probes on >15% of nodes in a slice
- Canary health-check failures (2 consecutive failed checks within 5 minutes)

If ACME signs off on these triggers we'll commit to the 2-hour rollback SLA and run a dry-run canary 48 hours before the window.

Neha Kapoor
Product Reliability, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: rollback_playbook.md excerpt]
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Harry Stevens <harry.stevens@acmehealth.com>, ACME IT Ops <ops-it@acmehealth.com>
Cc: DPO ACME <dpo@acmehealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed maintenance window and version pin plan for ACME private fleet

Thanks everyone — finalizing:

- Scheduled: 2026-12-04 01:00–05:00 ET (2026-12-04 06:00–10:00 UTC). Canary dry-run: 2026-12-02 02:00–03:00 ET.
- Window length: 4 hours as per Jonas. Post-window monitoring: 60 minutes mandatory, extended to 120 minutes if any marginal alerts fire.
- Rollback: pre-staged images & snapshots committed; we accept ACME 2-hour rollback SLA with the triggers Neha listed.
- Audit: logs will be written to ACME S3 at s3://acmehealth-inference-maintenance/2026-12-04/ with 90d lifecycle; DPO will receive the signed pointer and event digest within 6 hours post-window.

Next steps for ACME: please confirm (1) acceptance of window, (2) DPO acknowledgement on retention, (3) list of on-call contacts for the rollback runbook. Once we have that we will create INF-3421 subtask runbook and share the final doc links.

Final runbook (draft): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeF-acme-patches
Jira: INF-3421

Rachel
Technical Account Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: maintenance_risk_matrix.xlsx — final excerpt]
